# NOTES: THE WEIGHT OF THE CROWN (Fred M. White, 1904; Gutenberg #36511)

Single book, 49 chapters. Preface: illustrated; publisher R. F. Fenno & Co. (NY), Ward Lock & Co. (London), 1906. Illustrations: "She was going to have a look at the pictures"; "A stifled cry came from Jessie's lips" (ch IV); "What is it?" Jessie asked anxiously (ch VII); Ronald Hope trying to force brandy (ch XII); Another man struck the whistler (ch XXIII); Don't you make a sound (ch XXXIV); Dead white face of the King (ch XLIII).

## Cast
- **Jessie Harcourt**: beautiful shop-girl, fitter-on at Madame Malmaison's, Bond Street. Daughter of Colonel Harcourt (Royal Galways, Kent Harcourts), died penniless. Sister **Ada Harcourt** (delicate, paints, Christmas cards; lodgings near Oxford Street).
- **Madame Malmaison**: shrill, faded fair-haired proprietress, London-born.
- **Princess Mazaroff**, Russian; son **Prince Boris Mazaroff** (dissolute, kissed Jessie; falsely accused her). Later **Prince Mazaroff** is a Russian agent, arrested in Paris under another name.
- **Vera Galloway**: niece/adopted daughter of Lord and Lady Merehaven; lover **Charles Maxwell** (private secretary to Lord Merehaven). Look-alike of Jessie. Substitutes Jessie for her party. Run over by cab in Piccadilly, taken to Charing Cross Hospital (ankle injury), claims name Harcourt. Maid unnamed. Pet cats Tommy and Larry; "Lionel" a pet.
- **Ronald Hope**, Captain, Vera's cousin, Jessie's old sweetheart (secret game: "your heart and mine" with dog-rose petals). Served in Ireland, India; wants Asturian post via Maxgregor.
- **Lady Merehaven** (short-sighted, aunt of Vera); **Lord Merehaven** (Foreign Secretary, grey, old diplomat).
- **Queen Margaret of Asturia** (Queen; diamond tiara; "Duchess of Dinon" incognito; daughter of father's castle in hills). Lover/confidant **General Paul Maxgregor** (Scottish, Maxgregor of Glen; in Asturian service 20+ years; friend of Ronald; Varney's friend "doctor friend" who treated him).
- **King Erno of Asturia**: drunkard, gambler, red-haired, mean face; four years on throne, not crowned. Dissolute; drugged.
- **Dr. Varney**: distinguished physician, grey beard, shrewd; attended the King; knew Colonel Harcourt; former army doctor; sees through Jessie; gives permit.
- **Lechmere**: grey, lean, tall, greyhound-like former Queen's Messenger; diplomat-detective; "Moscow case"; Hotel Petersburg, 15 Nov 1897 (loo, one-eyed waiter).
- **Countess Saens** (Vera Olpheut, anarchist, morganatic wife of Russian grand duke claim; yellow satin; black eyes; Connaught Crescent house; killed husband; Russian spy). Maid **Annette** (Swiss, French-speaking; lover **Robert**, gentleman's servant/valet).
- **Hunt**: American editor of the **Evening Mercury** (Fleet Street, 191B); £2,000 + £5,000 cheque deal.
- **Eveleigh**: editor of the **Daily Herald** (sound, respectable paper).
- **Count Gleikstein**: Russian chargé d'affaires.
- **Sir Reginald (Reggie) Lancing**: old; son **Captain Dick Lancing** shot himself at club, papers.
- **Pongo** (Honourable George Lascelles): silly society young man with motor-car.
- **Peretori (Prince Peretori of Nassa)**: second cousin of King Erno, mad practical joker, master of disguise; wig of flame hair; won bet of 1,000 guineas; later drives to accident; sends telegram.
- **Pierre Loti**: peasant hut-dweller near Amiens accident site, paid 2,000 francs.
- **Captain Alexis**: king's escort.
- **Inspector Taske**; **Roscoe** (police inspector at Countess's house).
- **Dr. Salerno** (supplied drops); **Tomani** (faithful Asturian minister, cypher telegram).
- **Madame Peri** (diva singer). Miss Cheylesmere (girl who passed letter). Miss Maitland; Amy Macklin; Connie; Lady Longmarsh; Sheringham; Bannister (footman); Igon (associate of Mazaroff); Bevis (rented suite); Barlow (suite owner); Prince Alix (of Vienna, claimant to throne).
- Lady novelist, Lord Merehaven's secretary (unnamed young man).

## Plot events in order
**Ch I**: Jessie dismissed for alleged flirtation with Prince Boris (he kissed her in library, Princess complained; Madame Malmaison refuses to hear her). Receives letter (no heading/signature): asks her to 17 Gordon Gardens (Lady Merehaven's house), 9:30 pm, plainly dressed in black, thick veil, say she is "young person from Forder's in Piccadilly"; offers £500–£1,000. Ada encourages. Jessie meets Boris at New Bond Street; rebuffs him ("not an Englishman"). At No. 17 she finds reception/dinner; maid leads her to dressing-room; king carried by two women (Queen with tiara, and older grey-haired lady) along corridor. Vera Galloway appears, reveals likeness.

**Ch II**: Vera explains: King of Asturia is a scoundrel; Queen his protector; Vera substitutes Jessie. Ronald told Vera of Jessie. Vera's maid dismissed; swap of clothes. Jessie as Vera at party; Queen of Asturia asks her to take General Maxgregor into corridor sitting-room (next to dressing room where King lies). Jessie meets Boris at hall.

**Ch III**: Maxgregor arrives; Jessie leads him to room. Boris confronts Jessie at fountain; talks of queen, king, Charles Maxwell.

**Ch IV**: Ronald Hope appears, recognizes Jessie through rose-petal game; agrees to distract Boris (called away by Lord Merehaven's secretary). Ronald learns truth. Man in window (king) waves arms, nearly falls; saved.

**Ch V**: King drugged-awake, raving about red figure with knife; leaps at window; Maxgregor saves him. Queen and Maxgregor plan: Maxgregor's two bottles of drops from Dr. Salerno.

**Ch VI**: Jessie brings note-free message; Boris and Igon talk (king disappeared from gambling den; treaty for Russian passes to be signed). Jessie receives note: "At all hazards go up... warn the general... pull down the blind!"

**Ch VII**: Maxgregor reveals temptation to kill king; Jessie gives him pity. Maxgregor shot in shoulder through window (blind up).

**Ch VIII**: Jessie fetches Ronald; plan: Maxgregor swaps clothes with king, escapes in hansom; Jessie blocks fair woman spy in lane (sets off with cabman). Jessie gets supper; message from "Charing Cross Hospital": Vera injured. Jessie talks to king (king mumbles "Charleston Street, No. 15"). Queen returns.

**Ch IX**: Queen and Jessie talk; Pongo's motor-car in lane; Dr. Varney says Vera is in hospital.

**Ch X**: Varney spots Jessie's resemblance; confides; gives hospital permit. Jessie tells Varney her story (father Colonel Harcourt). Varney plans to keep secret.

**Ch XI**: Countess Saens's maid Annette accuses Jessie of burglary; Countess's papers stolen; Varney says Vera was the thief; advises black wrap. Newsboys: suicide of Captain Lancing; flight of Charles Maxwell.

**Ch XII**: Lechmere learns Countess's background from Saul Marx; Varney asks about Hunt of Evening Mercury. Footman: Sir Reginald Lancing collapses in study.

**Ch XIII**: Lechmere traces Hunt, learns Mercury had info at 6:50 pm (before the theft). Lord Merehaven: papers given to Lancing and Maxwell at seven.

**Ch XIV**: Countess meets Hunt at Carlton; wants £2,000; papers stolen; Hunt wants them. Countess plans to Charing Cross Hospital.

**Ch XV**: Hunt's plan: "reward £100." Countess sees hospital; Pongo drops Jessie at hospital; Jessie meets Maxwell at hospital.

**Ch XVI**: Lechmere's reasoning: papers sold to a woman (Countess). Varney sends Ronald to watch Mazaroff. Lechmere deduces Countess.

**Ch XVII**: Varney confronts the King (drug); King brought downstairs; Count Gleikstein arrives. Ronald writes card for queen; queen refuses to see visitor. King walks in: "His Majesty the King of Asturia!"

**Ch XVIII-XIX**: Maxwell and Jessie at hospital; Countess refused. Vera in hospital; papers lost after accident (cab in Piccadilly); Vera had received anonymous letter.

**Ch XX-XXI**: King's performance; Mazaroff and Gleikstein disconcerted; Lechmere's Moscow hint. Mazaroff gets Countess's letter, reads, tells Varney; Mazaroff accuses Jessie to Lord Merehaven in library.

**Ch XXII-XXIV**: Maxwell and Jessie see King in Countess's dining room; queen intervenes in library; Maxwell intercepts whistling man, takes Countess's card: "Key of the situation lies with General Maxgregor." Lechmere forges envelope; girl Cheylesmere gives it to Mazaroff.

**Ch XXV-XXVI**: Maxwell visits Maxgregor; they hide in dark; Mazaroff enters (CH XXVIII-XXIX) claiming wrong suite. Ronald and Jessie kiss; Jessie exhausted. Lechmere to Maxgregor.

**Ch XXVII-XXVIII**: Lechmere at Mercury office; gets advance copy from printer (£10 note). Mercury article: king abdicated, interview. Lechmere to Eveleigh of Herald, who will print refutation; Lechmere spots agony-column cypher referring to Peretori.

**Ch XXIX-XXXI**: Mazaroff in Maxgregor's room; Lechmere hides; Lechmere catches "Peretori" in suite of "Bevis"; Peretori's stick. Lechmere reads article to queen.

**Ch XXXII-XXXIV**: Lechmere plans special trains; Maxwell volunteers to go to Asturia. Lechmere confronts Peretori; reveals Peretori impersonated King for bet (1,000 guineas).

**Ch XXXV-XXXVII**: Peretori's telephone call; Annette tells Robert about papers hidden (found by policeman); Hunt arrives at Countess's; quarrel; Countess forged-ish telegram from Erno (sent by Peretori, signed "Erno," at Hotel Bristol Paris, "Mr. Conway").

**Ch XXXVIII-XL**: Jessie goes with Vera to hotel; Vera's ankle. Ronald and Jessie reunite; Jessie sends Ada message. Police inquire; Ronald gets Jessie into cab.

**Ch XLI-XLII**: Lechmere makes Annette identify Jessie as not the thief; Inspector Taske. Newsboys: King in train accident near Amiens. Countess returns to house.

**Ch XLIII-XLIV**: Lechmere to Poiteux; Loti; finds dead King hidden under straw in hut. Maxwell and Alexis hurt. Mazaroff drugs Maxwell's lemonade; arrested in Paris (warrant).

**Ch XLV-XLVI**: Lechmere brings body to Maxgregor's rooms; Varney certifies shock death. Queen receives Tomani cable ("King here safe"). Jessie deduces Peretori impersonated king in capital.

**Ch XLVII-XLVIII**: Merehaven visits queen; Countess arrested at carriage. Lechmere finds Deed of Abdication in king's dress coat; finds papers in plaster cast (Adoration of Magi/crucifix) in Annette's room.

**Ch XLIX**: Maxwell cleared; Lancing's letter exonerates. Mercury apology. King's death announced; Peretori impersonation. Queen to marry Maxgregor (ex-queen). Jessie and Ronald engaged; Vera and Maxwell reconciled.

## Key quotes/phrases
- "Uneasy lies the head" (ch VII title).
- "Foreforewarned, forearmed" (ch XXI).
- "I have said it!" (Peretori, ch XXXIX).
- Note on blind: "pull down the blind!"
- Mercury interview: "One of the most amazing romances in the history of Europe."
